# Dyadic coefficients for the positive rational pseudofermion approximation

These are the finite coefficients of [Theorem V.3.14a](../../../appendices/appendix_v_computational_programs.md), part IV. The continuous-spectrum approximation, coefficient-rounding, determinant and normalized total-variation proofs remain in that theorem.

<a id="coefficients"></a>
## Exact coefficients

The lattice mass and spectral interval are
$$
 m=\frac1{16},\qquad a=\frac1{256},\qquad b=\frac{16641}{256},
 \qquad \sqrt{ab}=\frac{129}{256}.
$$
There are $201$ poles, indexed by $j=-100,\ldots,100$, with $K=100$ and
$$
 h=178769486163447\,2^{-48},\qquad
 \widetilde t_j=a_j2^{b_j},\qquad \widetilde w_j=c_j2^{d_j},
 \qquad\widetilde r(x)=\sum_{j=-100}^{100}\frac{\widetilde w_j}{x+\widetilde t_j}.
$$
Every integer in the table is literal; these equations define exact dyadic rationals. The theorem's bound applies simultaneously for $V\le65536$ and complex matrix dimension $N=20V\le1310720$.
